questions.q: Why does integration code so often need to go asynchronous?
options: Because asynchronous Apex runs faster than synchronous Apex in every case
Because synchronous Apex cannot perform SOQL queries
Because a transaction can't make a callout while it has pending uncommitted DML, so saving a record and calling out about it usually need separate transactions
Because Platform Events require async Apex to be enabled org-wide
questions.explain: Async Apex resolves the callout-vs-DML ordering rule by giving the callout and the DML their own separate, chained transactions.

questions.q: What is a key limitation of @future(callout=true) methods compared to Queueable Apex?
options: Future methods always run synchronously
Future methods are deprecated and no longer supported
Future methods cannot make callouts at all
Future method parameters are limited to primitives and collections of primitives, not SObjects, and a future method can't chain into further async work
questions.explain: Future methods can't accept SObject parameters and can't enqueue further chained work, unlike Queueable Apex, which is a real object that can hold state and chain jobs.

questions.q: Which async mechanism is built for processing large record volumes in scoped chunks, with each chunk getting its own transaction and governor limits?
options: Batch Apex
@future methods
Platform Events
Scheduled Apex
questions.explain: Batch Apex's start/execute/finish model processes records in scoped chunks, with each execute invocation running in its own transaction.

questions.q: What distinguishes point-to-point asynchronous work (like Queueable or Batch Apex) from event-driven integration (like Platform Events)?
options: Point-to-point work always runs faster than event-driven integration
Point-to-point work explicitly enqueues a known next step; event-driven integration uses publish/subscribe where the publisher doesn't know who, if anyone, is listening
There is no real difference between the two styles
Event-driven integration can never be asynchronous
questions.explain: Point-to-point async is right when you know exactly what needs to happen next; event-driven integration decouples publishers from subscribers entirely.

questions.q: What is Scheduled Apex typically used for in an integration context?
options: Publishing Platform Events in real time as records are edited
Replacing Named Credentials for authentication
Triggering a Batch or Queueable integration job on a recurring, cron-like timer rather than in response to a specific user action
Generating a WSDL for a SOAP web service
questions.explain: Scheduled Apex provides cron-like recurring execution, commonly used to kick off a nightly or hourly Batch or Queueable integration job.
